title: integrate-ode-symplectic — structure-preserving integration of Hamiltonian systems
description:
Third slice of the ODE epic (parent: scientist-workbench-32z). Integrates Hamiltonian systems dq/dt = ∂H/∂p, dp/dt = −∂H/∂q where energy conservation over long integrations is essential. Standard methods (RKF45) drift in energy at O(t · h^p) for an order-p method; symplectic methods are bounded in energy error by O(h^p) regardless of integration length.

Use cases: orbital mechanics (planetary dynamics over Gyr), classical-mechanics talks (pendulum, double pendulum, n-body), molecular dynamics (NVE ensembles), plasma particle-in-cell, beam dynamics in accelerators.

Algorithms (in order of complexity):
- Velocity Verlet (2nd-order, the MD workhorse) — first to ship
- Leapfrog (2nd-order, dual to Verlet)
- Yoshida 4th-order (composition of three Verlet steps with Suzuki-Yoshida coefficients)
- Optionally: 6th-order Yoshida or symplectic Runge-Kutta (Radau-IIA on the augmented system) for high-precision orbital mechanics

Wire input: record{H: expression, q_vars: list<symbol>, p_vars: list<symbol>, q0: list<float64>, p0: list<float64>, t_span, n_steps, options?: record{order?: 2|4|6, scheme?: 'verlet'|'leapfrog'|'yoshida'}}.
Wire output: trajectory split into q and p; plus energy(t) array and energy_drift_max field for the agent to verify symplecticity at a glance.

Boundary tags: standard ODE three plus 'integrate-ode-symplectic/non-separable-hamiltonian' for H that doesn't decompose as T(p) + V(q) (Verlet-class methods require separability; non-separable Hs need implicit symplectic methods which are a much bigger build).
design: Algorithm: velocity Verlet for path-finder (Hairer-Lubich-Wanner 'Geometric Numerical Integration' §VI is the canonical reference). Substrate: extend packages/ode-core/ from the path-finder. Auto-derives ∂H/∂q, ∂H/∂p via cas-diff (the closed-vocabulary symbolic differentiation we already have). Bench tiers: A shape edges (1-DOF harmonic), B canonical (Kepler 2-body, simple pendulum, double pendulum, harmonic chain), C long-time (Kepler at 10^4 periods, energy bounded vs RKF45 unbounded — the discriminator vs the IVP slice), D non-separable detection (H = (q+p)^2/2 should boundary-tag), E boundary (NaN H, malformed q0/p0 dim mismatch). Reference oracle: hand-coded velocity Verlet in Python + analytic Kepler conserved quantities (H, L) for verification.
acceptance_criteria: bench/integrate-ode-symplectic/ scaffold complete; Verlet reference implementation in Python passes bench; tools/integrate-ode-symplectic/ ships seven artefacts; bun run check green; bench 100% pass with energy-drift verification on Kepler 2-body over 10^4 orbital periods

Reference hand-coded velocity Verlet via sympy autodiff passes verifier 17/17. Verifier headline check: energy_drift_not_secular on long-time tier — the discriminator vs non-symplectic. Tagged: degenerate-tspan, non-separable-hamiltonian (verifier re-checks via sympy), non-finite-during-eval. Output adds energy_drift_max + energy_drift_secular fields.

title: tools/linalg-equiv: numerical analogue of cas-verify (equal-within-tolerance)
description: Numerical analogue of cas-verify. Decides whether two SolveResult records (or, generally, two records of the same shape with float64 leaves) are equal-within-tolerance. Schema: input record{lhs, rhs, rtol?, atol?}; output record{equal: boolean, max_abs_diff: float64, max_rel_diff: float64, where?: string}. Boundary categories per ADR-0003: malformed inputs (different shapes, non-finite leaves) raise ToolError; equality decisions are routine non-success per the record-with-flag pattern. Forces ADR-0015's "cross-platform numerical evidence" framing into a concrete tool: cross-platform records that pass linalg-equiv are evidence of agreement up to tolerance even when output_hashes differ. title: Design run() ergonomic surface bridging q0b output to sturm-execute + sturm-sample
description:
Spec v3 §5.2 defines run<F>(f, opts): Promise<RunResult<F>> returning {output: ResolveClassical<ReturnType<F>>, measurements, shots}. This shape predates ADR-0007's distribution-vs-sampling split — the workbench factored execution into sturm-execute (analytic distribution) and sturm-sample (per-shot resolutions given entropy).

q0b (sturm-trace) emits only IR. A user-facing run() needs additional plumbing: take q0b's IR output, pipe through sturm-execute, optionally pipe through sturm-sample, then reconstruct RunResult<O> by mapping the IR's classical_ref strings back to the user's Classical<T> brand handles (correspondence established at trace time).

Approach — decide and document:
1. Where the bridge lives:
   a. A new tool sturm-run that composes sturm-trace | sturm-execute | sturm-sample into a single invocation.
   b. A user-facing TS function run() exported from packages/sturm-trace-runtime/ (the runtime package q0b will spawn) that does the composition in-process.
   c. Leave it to userland — agents compose by-pipe with no convenience wrapper.
2. How RunResult<O>.measurements: Map<ClassicalRef, boolean> is reconstructed from sturm-sample's samples: list<record> output. The mapping between TS-side Classical<T> brand handles and IR-side classical_ref strings is established at trace time.
3. Whether this is q0b-blocking or a follow-up.

This issue is q0b-adjacent but not strictly required for q0b's 'trace-only' v0.1. Filed separately to surface the design question before q0b implementation begins; may be folded into q0b's body or absorbed into the runtime package issue once the call is made.

title: expr-parse self-test: compare via canonicalize, not JSON.stringify
description:
tools/expr-parse/tool.ts:309-312 round-trips through parseValue(JSON.stringify(...)) to compare two values structurally. This works only because both sides happen to be re-parsed from JSON; under any non-canonical key ordering it would silently break.

Use canonicalize(a) === canonicalize(b) — that'\''s exactly what the protocol guarantees structural equality means.

title: expr-parse: avoid string += in number/identifier accumulators

V8 worst case is O(n²) on these shapes. Use start-index + slice: let start = this.pos; while (...) this.pos++; const intPart = this.src.slice(start, this.pos).

title: Decide fpInv vs Fermat in NTT plan-build
description:
packages/mod-core/src/ntt.ts:74-80 (fpInv) calls modInv (extended Euclid, generic for any modulus) even though p = 998244353 is prime. Fermat'\''s little theorem (a^(p-2) mod p) is simpler and removes the dependency on the ModInvResult shape (modular.ts:31-38) inside the NTT core.

Options: (a) inline Fermat in fpInv and keep the dependency local; (b) keep the modInv call and document why (consistency with the modular package). Either is fine — choose and comment.

title: ADR pinning Exp representation and migration to dense vectors
description:
packages/cas-core/src/poly.ts:33-77 uses Exp = ReadonlyArray<readonly [string, number]>, with expKey = JSON.stringify(e) as the Map key. polyMul (poly.ts:113-132) is O(|a|×|b|) with a JSON serialisation per key access. Fine for (x+1)(x-1); will collapse on Buchberger over a 5-variable system, polynomial GCD, or factoring — anything one would actually use a CAS for.

Don'\''t fix now. File ADR-0005 pinning the current representation as a known wart with the planned migration: either Map<varName, exponent> per monomial with precomputed degVec, or fixed-variable-order Uint32Array exponent vectors (what every serious CAS uses). Decision triggers when cas-reduce or Gröbner work begins.
acceptance_criteria: ADR-0005 filed, references current poly.ts code, names the trigger for migration, lists candidate representations with tradeoffs

title: Lazy path reconstruction in protocol error paths
description:
canonical.ts and validate.ts allocate and spread path arrays on every recursive call: [...path, key] at canonical.ts:17, 27 and validate.ts:115, 126, 138, 144. The path is only consumed when an error throws — never on the happy path.

Two cleaner shapes: (a) carry a parent link (linked list) and reconstruct path on throw; (b) carry a depth counter + a reusable scratch buffer. Either way, eliminate per-recursion allocation.
acceptance_criteria: No path-array allocation on the happy path; ProtocolError messages still include the dotted path on failure; existing tests pass

title: encodeString: avoid quadratic string concat
description:
packages/protocol/src/canonical.ts:46-62. Loop builds the result with out += s.charAt(i) for every character. V8 has worst-case O(n²) behaviour for some string-concat shapes; a hot-path encoder for canonical bytes should not be exposed to it.

Replace with parts.push(...) + parts.join('\'''\''), or use String.prototype.replace over the seven escape characters in a single pass.
acceptance_criteria: encodeString uses a non-quadratic strategy; round-trip test passes; spot-benchmark on a 100KB string shows linear scaling

title: F9: TDD discipline doc — distinguish 'spec from scratch' from 'port and verify'
description:
Symptom: README's 'writing a new tool' section assumes pure RED→GREEN. When porting a known-good algorithm (as we did with NTT), the cycle is: write impl, write tests, mutation-prove tests catch regressions. Both are valid TDD-shaped workflows but the discipline is different.

Fix: add a section to README (or a new docs/CONTRIBUTING.md) describing both flows: 'Port and verify' vs 'Spec from scratch.' Include the mutation-prove technique (deliberately break the impl, confirm tests go RED, restore).
notes: Resolved 2026-04-28. CLAUDE.md adds 'Two TDD shapes — both valid': spec-from-scratch (classic RED→GREEN) vs port-and-verify (port → comprehensive tests → mutation-prove + cross-validate). The mutation-prove technique replaces the literal RED-first step when porting a known-good algorithm. Honesty rule: 'tests have caught a real regression' is the principle, not 'the test was committed before the impl.'

title: cas-core polynomial GCD: modular / sparse modular as v0.2
description: ADR-0013 landed Brown-Collins subresultant PRS as the v0.1 polynomial GCD. The follow-up: modular GCD (Brown's algorithm for univariate over Z; Brown-Yun-EZ-style for multivariate) for performance on dense or sparse inputs. Subresultant has polynomial coefficient bounds but no asymptotic edge over modular methods, and modular methods are dramatically faster on adversarial inputs (high-degree dense polynomials, large coefficient bit-widths). Implementation requires: prime selection / bound estimation, bad-prime detection (degree drop on reduction), CRT reconstruction, leading-coefficient lifting for multivariate. Defer until a workload demands it.
acceptance_criteria: packages/cas-core/src/poly-gcd-modular.ts (or similar) implements at least univariate Brown's; benchmark shows 10× or better on stress inputs (large coefficients, degree-50 univariate); both algorithms agree on correctness; existing subresultant kept as fallback for cases the modular path rejects.

THE TWO PRINCIPLES (universal decision rule for scientist-workbench, stated by the user 2026-05-04 as the highest-priority framework, supersedes any other framing):

1. What would a TypeScript expert expect/want?
2. It must be irresistible to agents (who are TS experts).

These are the same principle viewed from two sides: the agent IS the TS expert, so what (1) says is what (2) requires.

WHY: cited twice in the same session — first directing cas-diff's design, then again as a closing reminder after the tier-1 vocabulary extension shipped. It supersedes any other framework: "decomposition discipline," "honest scope," "agent-honest output" are *consequences* of the two principles, not separate axioms.

HOW TO APPLY:
- When in doubt, take a position. Don't escalate questions where the principles produce a clear answer.
- Apply them in commit messages and worklog "why" sections.
- Operational test: "a TS expert would type this without thinking" should be defensible. If it needs a paragraph of justification, the design is probably wrong.

CONCRETE EXAMPLES from this session:
- cas-diff input shape `{f, var}` (mirrors integrate-1d, predictable)
- cas-diff vocabulary matches integrate-1d/optimize, not cas-simplify (compose without scope translation)
- Tier-1 head naming: `asin`/`acos`/`atan` (matches Math.* — what TS reaches for reflexively)
- Smart constructors only in cas-diff, no internal cas-simplify call (one tool, one operation)

WRONG FRAMES TO AVOID:
- "What does Mathematica/SymPy do?" — irrelevant unless coincides with TS-expert want
- "What's the most general API?" — irrelevant if not what agent reaches for
- "What's the smallest surface?" — irrelevant if it forces caller assembly

SUBAGENTS ARE NOT THE DEFAULT. When a task is mechanical and well-specified by the principles, just do the work. Wrapping mechanical edits in a subagent prompt is a way of delegating the application of the principles, which the user has rejected (observed 2026-05-04: rejected subagent dispatch for tier-1 vocab extension; right move was to apply principles and edit directly). Subagents are for genuinely parallel independent work and contested-design research (CLAUDE.md Rule 4), not coordination overhead for routine implementation.

NARROWER COMPANION AXIOM: feedback_ts_native_design.md (auto-memory) and ADR-0009 — sturm-specific "don't port Julia idioms to TS." That memory predates the explicit universal statement of the two principles; it's a consequence of them applied to the sturm DSL design.

Coding subagents in scientist-workbench use Opus, not Sonnet. WHY: stated by user 2026-05-05 during ODE bench planning. HOW TO APPLY: when spawning Agent for implementation work (tool construction, package code, refactor), pass model='opus'. Research/read-only subagents (codebase queries, audits, exploration) using sonnet is fine — the rule is specifically about *coding*. Two principles consequence: a TS expert wants the strongest model on the actual implementation surface; subagent quality compounds with bench rigor.
